s: Who among the following poets of Krishnadevaraya's court wrote Bhava Chinta Ratna and Veerasaivamrita in Kannada?
x: Mallanarya of Krishnadevaraya's court wrote Bhava Chinta Ratna and Veerasaivamrita in Kannada.

s: What special honour did Krishnadevaraya himself bestow on Allasani Peddana?
o: He appointed him governor of Chandragiri.
He fixed the Gandapenderam anklet on Peddana's foot.
He made him commander of the Arab cavalry.
x: Krishnadevaraya personally fixed the Gandapenderam anklet on Allasani Peddana's foot.

s: With which poet is the dvyarthi kavya (poem with double meaning) associated?
x: Dvyarthi kavya is associated with Pingali Surana; Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu wrote Ramabhyudayamu.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Panduranga Mahatmyam was written by Tenali Ramakrishna. Pingali Surana wrote Raghava Pandaviyamu and Kalapurnodayamu.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Pingali Surana — Raghava Pandaviyamu and Kalapurnodayamu
x: Pingali Surana wrote Raghava Pandaviyamu and Kalapurnodayamu. The other works belong to Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu, Ramarajabhushana and Allasani Peddana respectively.

s: Which Ashtadiggaja poet, titled 'Andhra Kavita Pitamaha', wrote Manucharitramu?
x: Allasani Peddana wrote Manucharitramu (Swarochisha Manu Sambhavam) and was titled Andhra Kavita Pitamaha.

s: By what name does the Tippalur inscription refer to the Ashtadiggajas?
x: The Tippalur inscription calls them the 'Kavula Samstha' (institution of poets); Bhuvana Vijayam was the court hall where they met.

s: Parijatapaharanamu was written by which Ashtadiggaja?
x: Nandi Timmana, known as Mukku Timmana, wrote Parijatapaharanamu.

s: Who among the following had the title 'Prabandha Parameshwara'?
x: Prabandha Parameshwara is Errana's title, not Nandi Timmana's.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Ashtadiggajas:
1. Dhurjati wrote Sri Kalahasteeswara Mahatyam.
2. Nandi Timmana bore the title Prabandha Parameshwara.
3. Pingali Surana wrote Raghava Pandaviyamu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Prabandha Parameshwara is Errana's title; Nandi Timmana was called Mukku Timmana.

s: Who wrote Vasucharitramu, dedicated to Tirumala Raya?
x: Ramarajabhushana (Bhattumurti) wrote Vasucharitramu and Narasabhupaliyamu.

s: What is the literal meaning of 'Bhuvana Vijayam'?
x: Bhuvana Vijayam means 'conquest of the world'; Ashtadiggajas means eight elephants and Kavula Samstha institution of poets.

s: Which Vijayanagara king granted the Tippalur agrahara (Kadapa) to the Ashtadiggajas?
x: The Tippalur inscription records Krishnadevaraya's gift of Tippalur agrahara to the Ashtadiggajas, whom he patronised.

s: Who wrote Ramabhyudayamu?
x: Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu, one of the Ashtadiggajas, wrote Ramabhyudayamu, the Ramayana in Telugu.

s: By what popular name was the Ashtadiggaja poet Nandi Timmana known?
x: Nandi Timmana, author of Parijatapaharanamu, was called Mukku Timmana.

s: By what other name was the poet Ramarajabhushana known?
x: Ramarajabhushana, author of Vasucharitramu and Narasabhupaliyamu, was also called Bhattumurti.

s: Krishnadevaraya's reign is regarded as the golden age of which literature?
x: His reign, with the Ashtadiggajas, is called the golden age of Telugu literature (the Prabandha era).

s: By what name is the period of Telugu literature under Krishnadevaraya known?
x: Krishnadevaraya's reign is the Prabandha era, the golden age of Telugu literature.

s: By what other name was the Bhuvana Vijayam of Krishnadevaraya's court known?
x: Bhuvana Vijayam is identified as the House of Victory and formed part of the royal courtly setting described by travellers.

s: What is the literal meaning of the title 'Amuktamalyada'?
o: One who wears the garland of victory
One who offers the garland she has worn
One who conquers the garlanded city
One who worships Vishnu with flowers
x: Amuktamalyada means “one who offers the garland she has worn,” referring to the devotional story associated with Goda Devi or Andal.

s: During which campaign did Krishnadevaraya write Amuktamalyada?
x: It was written during the Kalinga campaign after Andhra Mahavishnu of Srikakulam commanded him in a dream; it is dedicated to Lord Venkateswara.

s: The phrase “Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa” occurs in which work?
x: The famous expression praising Telugu among regional languages occurs in the preface to Amuktamalyada.

s: Amuktamalyada, one of the Telugu Pancha Kavyas, is the first Telugu work named after whom?
x: It is named after its heroine, Goda Devi, not its author.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Usha Parinayam is among the Sanskrit works attributed to Krishnadevaraya. Amuktamalyada is Telugu, while Jambavati Kalyanam and Rasamanjari are Sanskrit.

s: Which was Krishnadevaraya's only Telugu work?
x: Madalasa Charita, Rasamanjari, Jnana Chintamani and Satyavadhu Parinayam are Sanskrit; Amuktamalyada is his only Telugu work.

s: According to legend, which deity told Krishnadevaraya in a dream to write Amuktamalyada?
x: The legend says Andhra Mahavishnu of Srikakulam (Krishna district) appeared in a dream during the Kalinga campaign.

s: With whom does Amuktamalyada narrate the marriage of Goda Devi (Andal)?
x: Its theme is Goda Devi (Andal) and her marriage to Sri Ranganatha; the work is dedicated to Venkateswara.

s: By what other name is Amuktamalyada known?
x: Amuktamalyada is also called Vishnuchittiyam; the other three are works of the Ashtadiggajas.

s: With reference to Amuktamalyada, which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Yamunacharya Charitra – A story included in the work
Genealogy from Bukka to Krishnadevaraya – Recorded in the work
Kingship and administration – Political advice given in the work
x: Amuktamalyada deals with Goda Devi's marriage to Ranganatha, includes the Yamunacharya Charitra and gives political advice on kingship; it does NOT record a genealogy from Bukka to Krishnadevaraya (APPSC G2 2003).

s: Which of the following works of Krishnadevaraya is NOT in Sanskrit?
x: Amuktamalyada is his only Telugu work; Madalasa Charita, Rasamanjari and Usha Parinayam are in Sanskrit.

s:
Consider the following statements about Amuktamalyada:
1. It records the genealogy of the dynasty from Bukka to Krishnadevaraya.
2. It contains references to the campaigns of Krishnadevaraya.
3. It discusses statecraft (rajaniti) and kingship.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Amuktamalyada refers to Krishnadevaraya's campaigns and gives political maxims on rajaniti and kingship, but it does not record a genealogy from Bukka (APPSC G2 2003).

s: To which deity did Krishnadevaraya dedicate Amuktamalyada?
x: Amuktamalyada was written at the bidding of Andhra Mahavishnu of Srikakulam but dedicated to Lord Venkateswara.

s: What was the mother tongue of the Tuluva ruling family?
x: Kannada was the mother tongue of the Tuluva family, whose progenitor was Timmaraju; Telugu was nonetheless favoured at court.

s: Who was the real ruler under Immadi Narasimha?
x: Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, a Saluva general, was the real ruler under Immadi Narasimha.

s: Who was the Prime Minister of Krishnadevaraya, popularly known as Appaji?
x: Saluva Timmarusu, popularly known as Appaji, served as the Prime Minister of Krishnadevaraya.

s: Whom did Krishnadeva Raya succeed in 1509?
x: Krishnadeva Raya succeeded Vira Narasimha, who began the Tuluva dynasty; the Saluva dynasty was founded by Narasimha Saluva.

s: Which of the following pairs (dynastic transition – ruler) is correctly matched?
o: Maurya to Shunga – Tirumala Deva Raya
x: Vira Narasimha began Tuluva rule, replacing the Saluvas. Narasimha Saluva ended Sangama rule, Tirumala Deva Raya began Aravidu rule and Pushyamitra Shunga replaced the Mauryas.

s: Who was the founder of the Tuluva dynasty?
x: Vira Narasimha, son of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, killed Immadi Narasimha in 1505 and founded the Tuluva dynasty; Narasa Nayaka was only a general and regent.

s: Who was the rajaguru of Krishnadevaraya?
x: The Madhva saint Vyasatirtha (Vyasaraya) was Krishnadevaraya's rajaguru; Purandaradasa was his disciple.

s: Who among the following, called the father of Carnatic music, was a disciple of Vyasatirtha and a contemporary of Krishnadevaraya?
x: Purandaradasa, disciple of Krishnadevaraya's rajaguru Vyasatirtha, lived in Krishnadevaraya's time; Tyagaraja and Kshetrayya came much later.

s: Who began the rule of the Aravidu dynasty of Vijayanagara?
x: Tirumala Deva Raya began Aravidu rule after the Tuluva line ended with Sadasiva.

s: Who praised Krishnadevaraya in the Tuzuk-i-Baburi?
x: Babur praised Krishnadevaraya in the Tuzuk-i-Baburi.

s: Which statement regarding the rulers preceding Saluva Narasimha is correct?
o: Praudha Raya was the general who seized the throne for Saluva Narasimha.
Virupaksha II was described as a drunkard, while Praudha Raya was considered worthless.
Virupaksha II founded the Saluva dynasty, while Praudha Raya ruled from Chandragiri.
Both rulers successfully repelled the Gajapati and Bahmani invasions.
x: Nuniz described Virupaksha II as a drunkard, while Praudha Raya was considered worthless; their weakness contributed to the crisis of the kingdom.

s: Where did Vira Narasimha kill Immadi Narasimha, the last Saluva ruler, in 1505?
x: The second usurpation took place at Penugonda, where Vira Narasimha killed Immadi Narasimha and began the Tuluva dynasty.

s: Whom did Saluva Narasimha expel in the first usurpation of 1485?
x: Saluva Narasimha of Chandragiri expelled Praudha Raya in 1485, ending the Sangama dynasty.

s: In which year did the second usurpation, which began the Tuluva dynasty, take place?
x: The second usurpation was in 1505; the first (Saluva) was in 1485.

s: By what other name is the Battle of Talikota known?
x: Talikota (1565) is also called Rakshasi-Tangadi or Bannihatti.

s: From where did Saluva Narasimha bring Arab horses?
x: Saluva Narasimha brought Arab horses from Ormuz and introduced Samugaris (gunmen).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Rajanatha Dindima, court poet of Saluva Narasimha, wrote Saluvabhyudayam. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam, not Saluvabhyudayam; Dhurjati wrote Sri Kalahasteeswara Mahatyam and Satakam, not Madhura Vijayam; Ramabhyudayamu is by Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu, while Tirumalamba wrote Varadambika Parinayam.

s: Saluva Narasimha lost Udayagiri to which Gajapati ruler?
x: Saluva Narasimha lost Udayagiri to Gajapati Purushottama; Krishnadevaraya later won it back from Prataparudra.

s: To which place did Saluva Narasimha move his capital from Kalyanapuram?
x: Saluva Narasimha's capital shifted from Kalyanapuram to Chandragiri.

s: Who wrote Saluvabhyudayam, the work on Saluva Narasimha?
x: Rajanatha Dindima was Saluva Narasimha's court poet and wrote Saluvabhyudayam.

s: Annamacharya, who composed 32,000 kirtanas on Lord Venkateswara, was a contemporary of which Vijayanagara ruler?
x: Annamacharya (1408-1503) lived in the time of Saluva Narasimha (1485-91); he died before Krishnadevaraya was crowned in 1509.

s: Krishnadevaraya was crowned on 8 August of which year?
x: The Hampi inscription dates his coronation to 8 August 1509.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a title of Krishnadevaraya?
x: Andhra Bhoja, Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma and Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana were titles of Krishnadevaraya. Gajabetekara (elephant hunter) was the title of the Sangama ruler Devaraya II.

s: Which of the following is NOT a title associated with Krishnadevaraya?
x: Andhra Kavita Pitamaha was the title conferred on Allasani Peddana. The other three are titles of Krishnadevaraya.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Nagalapuram was named after Krishnadevaraya's mother Nagalamba.

s: After whom was Hospet, also called Tirumaladevipattana, named?
x: Krishnadevaraya named Hospet after his queen Tirumaladevi.

s: Who among the following had the title 'Gajabetekara'?
x: Gajabetekara is Devaraya II's title and is a common decoy among Krishnadevaraya's titles.

s: What do Krishnadevaraya's titles 'Andhra Bhoja' and 'Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma' reflect?
x: Both titles honour Krishnadevaraya as a patron of letters, like King Bhoja.

s: Which campaign resulted in the defeat of Yusuf Adil Khan?
x: During the Diwani or Kovilkonda campaign of 1509–10, the Bahmani jihad was crushed and Yusuf Adil Khan was killed.

s: With which campaign of Krishnadevaraya is the title 'Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya' associated?
x: After taking Raichur and freeing Sultan Mahmud Shah from Ali Barid, Krishnadevaraya acquired the title Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Ummattur campaign?
o: Gangaraja was defeated and a new province was established at Srirangapatna.
Yusuf Adil Khan was killed and the Bahmani jihad was crushed.
The Balakrishna idol was brought to Hampi.
Victory pillars were erected at Potnuru and Simhachalam.
x: In the Ummattur or Sivasamudram campaign of 1512–13, Gangaraja was defeated and a new province was established at Srirangapatna.

s: In which year did Krishnadevaraya take Gulbarga?
x: After routing Ismail Adil Shah at Raichur in 1520, he took Gulbarga in 1523.

s: Krishnadevaraya earned the title Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya by freeing which Sultan from Ali Barid?
x: In the Raichur-Bidar campaign of 1510 he restored the Bahmani Sultan Mahmud Shah, freeing him from Ali Barid.

s: In which year did Krishnadevaraya defeat Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur in the Battle of Raichur?
x: In the Battle of Raichur (1520) Krishnadevaraya routed Ismail Adil Shah with Portuguese help; Gulbarga followed in 1523.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Yusuf Adil Khan was killed in Krishnadevaraya's Kovilkonda campaign.
2. Ismail Adil Shah was routed at Raichur in 1520 with Portuguese help.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Yusuf Adil Khan fell in the Kovilkonda (Diwani) campaign of 1509-10 and Ismail Adil Shah was routed at Raichur in 1520, so both are correct.

s: After a siege of how long did Udayagiri fall during Krishnadevaraya's Kalinga campaign?
x: Udayagiri fell after an 18-month siege in the Kalinga campaign of 1513-1519.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ummattur — Balakrishna idol taken to Hampi
x: After the conquest of Kondaveedu, Krishnadevaraya performed Talapurusha Danam at Amaravati. The other pairs associate results with the wrong campaigns.

s: Where did Krishnadevaraya set up his victory pillars?
x: Victory pillars were erected at Potnuru and Simhachalam after the Kalinga campaign. The pillar at Potnuru marked the conquest of coastal Andhra.

s: Whose daughter did Krishnadevaraya marry after the Kalinga campaign?
x: Prataparudra Gajapati gave his daughter to Krishnadevaraya, and lands north of the Krishna went back to the Gajapati.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Simhachalam — diamond necklace to Varaha Narasimha
Potnuru — pillar marking the conquest of coastal Andhra
Mangalagiri — land grant to Lakshmi Narasimha
Udayagiri — land grant to Lakshmi Narasimha
x: Udayagiri is associated with the capture of the Balakrishna idol. The land grant to Lakshmi Narasimha was made at Mangalagiri.

s: Which coastal places were known for salt, with salt pans at one of them being taxed?
o: Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam; the salt pans at Pedaganjam were taxed
Potnuru and Simhachalam; the salt pans at Simhachalam were taxed
Bhatkal and Raichur; the salt pans at Bhatkal were taxed
Kondaveedu and Kondapalli; the salt pans at Kondaveedu were taxed
x: Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam were known for salt, and the salt pans at Pedaganjam were taxed.

s: In which year did Krishnadevaraya's Kalinga campaign reach Cuttack?
x: Cuttack was reached in 1518 and the Gajapati sued for peace.

s: Under the peace with Prataparudra Gajapati, which lands went back to the Gajapati?
x: Prataparudra gave his daughter in marriage, and the lands north of the Krishna were returned to him.

s: At which temple did Krishnadevaraya present a diamond necklace to Varaha Narasimha?
x: He gave a diamond necklace at Simhachalam; at Mangalagiri he gave land to Lakshmi Narasimha.

s: Where did Krishnadevaraya perform the Talapurusha Danam after taking Kondaveedu?
x: Kondaveedu was taken with Saluva Timmarusu's help, after which the king performed Talapurusha Danam at Amaravati.

s: With whose help did Krishnadevaraya take the Kondaveedu fort by splitting Veerabhadra Gajapati's army?
x: Kondaveedu was taken with the help of Prime Minister Saluva Timmarusu, who split Veerabhadra Gajapati's army.

s: What does Gangadevi's Madhura Vijayam describe?
o: The marriage of Achyutaraya and Varadambika
x: Gangadevi, queen of Kumara Kampana, wrote Madhura Vijayam on Kampana's conquest of Madurai.

s: Which of the following pairs (poet – work) is correctly matched?
x: Tirumalamba wrote Varadambika Parinayam; Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.

s: What kind of Sanskrit work is Tirumalamba's Varadambika Parinayam?
x: Varadambika Parinayam is a Sanskrit champu.

s: Who made peace after Sadasiva and Rama Raya defeated Governor Martin de Souza for damaging temples?
x: João de Castro made peace after the defeat of Martin de Souza, whose actions had included damaging temples.

s: Vira Narasimha entered into an alliance with which Portuguese Viceroy for securing horses and military training?
x: Vira Narasimha allied with Viceroy Francisco de Almeida for horses and military training.

s: Where did Krishnadevaraya permit the Portuguese to build a fort for their support to Albuquerque in capturing Goa?
x: Krishnadevaraya received horses and military training and allowed the Portuguese a fort at Bhatkal.

s: Which Portuguese governor captured Goa from Bijapur in 1510 with Krishnadevaraya's backing?
x: Through his envoy Luis, Krishnadevaraya backed Albuquerque's capture of Goa from Bijapur in 1510.

s: Which foreign traveller, besides Domingo Paes, is associated with a visit to Krishnadevaraya’s court?
x: Barbosa also visited the court of Krishnadevaraya; Domingo Paes described the Bhuvana Vijayam or House of Victory and the king.

s: Which foreign traveller described the looks of Krishnadevaraya and the beauty of the city?
x: Domingo Paes described Krishnadevaraya's appearance and the beauty of the city. Duarte Barbosa also visited Vijayanagara, but the stated description is attributed to Paes.

s: During the reign of which ruler did the Portuguese traveller Fernao Nuniz visit Vijayanagara?
x: Nuniz wrote about Krishnadevaraya's rise but actually visited Vijayanagara under Achyutaraya.

s: Who was the last ruler of the Tuluva dynasty?
x: Sadasiva was the last Tuluva ruler; the usurpations were by Saluva Narasimha (1485) and Vira Narasimha (1505).

s: In which year was the Battle of Talikota fought?
x: The Battle of Talikota was fought in January 1565; Rama Raya was beheaded in it.

s: Venkatavilasa Mantapam was the assembly hall of which Vijayanagara king?
x: Achyutaraya's hall was the Venkatavilasa Mantapam; Krishnadevaraya's was the Bhuvana Vijayam.

s: Which Vijayanagara king was the only one crowned at Tirumala (Tirupati)?
x: Achyutaraya was crowned at Tirupati (and Srikalahasti); Nuniz visited during his reign.

s: How was Aliya Rama Raya related to Krishnadevaraya?
o: maternal uncle from the Gajapati family
younger brother from the Tuluva family
x: Aliya Rama Raya was Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law and belonged to the Aravidu family.

s: Where did Sadasiva and Tirumala flee after Rama Raya was beheaded at Talikota (1565)?
x: After Talikota, Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to Penukonda.

s: To which year do the Sadasivakona inscriptions found by the ASI in June 2026 belong?
x: The trilingual (Telugu, Tamil, Kannada) inscriptions are of 1554 CE and record Sadasiva Raya's holy bath and a transfer of Kaanika taxes.

s: Aliya Rama Raya killed which rival in 1543 before making Sadasiva a figurehead?
x: Rama Raya killed Salakam Tirumala in 1543 and made Sadasiva a figurehead.

s: Aliya Rama Raya belonged to which family?
x: Aliya Rama Raya, Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law, was of the Aravidu family.

s: Where were the three trilingual Sadasivakona inscriptions of 1554 CE found by the ASI in June 2026?
x: The Sadasivakona inscriptions were found in the Seshachalam forest of Tirupati district.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Sadasivakona inscriptions:
1. They are written in Telugu, Tamil and Kannada.
2. They record the transfer of Kaanika taxes from Gudimallam temple lands.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The three 1554 CE inscriptions are trilingual (Telugu, Tamil, Kannada) and record Sadasiva Raya's holy bath and the transfer of Kaanika taxes from Gudimallam temple lands.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Rayavachakam is correct?
o: It records nine departments, each headed by a Samprati.
It records twelve departments, each headed by a Karanika.
It records only military offices under the Mahapradhani.
It records four departments, each headed by a Dalavayi.
x: Rayavachakam records nine departments, and each department was headed by a Samprati.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Mahapradhani was the chief minister who headed the pradhanis. Karanikas were scribes, Rayasams were secretaries and the Dalavayi was the commander-in-chief.

s: Which matters did the Athavane department deal with in Vijayanagara administration?
x: Athavane was the revenue department; Kandachara was military and Bhandara the treasury.

s: Which of the following pairs (department – function) is correctly matched?
x: Bhandara was the treasury; Athavane was revenue, Kandachara military and Dharmasana judicial.

s: What was the chief minister heading the pradhanis in Vijayanagara called?
x: The Mahapradhani headed the pradhanis (e.g. Saluva Timmarusu); the Dalavayi was commander-in-chief.

s: According to the Rayavachakam, how many departments were there in the Vijayanagara administration?
x: The Rayavachakam records nine departments, each headed by a Samprati.

s: Who headed the Kandachara department of the Vijayanagara administration?
x: Kandachara was the military department; it was headed by the Senapati or Dalavayi, the commander-in-chief.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Department)
a. Kandachara
b. Athavane
c. Bhandara
d. Dharmasana
List-II (Function)
1. Treasury
2. Military
3. Justice
4. Revenue
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Kandachara dealt with military affairs, Athavane with revenue, Bhandara was the treasury and Dharmasana the judicial department.

s: What was the land assigned by the Vijayanagara king to military chiefs in lieu of cash salaries called?
x: Amaram was land granted to military chiefs, who were known as Amaranayakas, Nayaks, Palaiyagars or Poligars. The grant substituted for direct cash payment to the chiefs.

s: What title did the Vijayanagara amaranayakas hold?
x: Amaranayakas held the title Mahamandaleshwara and had more autonomy than the Durgadannayakas.

s: At which festival did Vijayanagara amaranayakas attend court with gifts?
x: Amaranayakas paid tribute, kept troops, horses and elephants, and attended court at Mahanavami with gifts.

s: What was the tribute paid by the Vijayanagara amaranayakas to the king called?
x: Amaranayakas paid tribute called Kappam and kept troops, horses and elephants for the king.

s: What was the principal political outcome of the Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara system after 1565?
o: The replacement of Nayakas by hereditary village accountants
The conversion of all amarams into Mughal jagirs
The complete abolition of regional chieftaincies
The emergence of semi-independent and later independent Nayaka states such as Madurai, Tanjore and Keladi
x: After 1565, semi-independent Nayaka kingdoms emerged and some became independent, including those of Madurai, Tanjore and Keladi.

s: Which of the following pairs (system – characteristic) is correctly matched?
o: Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara – Amaram fiefs and about 200 Nayakas
Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara – Numerical zat and sawar ranks
Mughal Mansabdari – Mandalams and forts held by 75 or 77 Nayakas
Kakatiya Nayankara – Amaram fiefs and about 200 Nayakas
x: The Vijayanagara system involved amaram fiefs and about 200 Nayakas. The Kakatiya system had 75 or 77 Nayakas holding mandalams and forts, and Mughal mansabdars held zat and sawar ranks.

s: Who is identified as the originator of the Kakatiya Nayankara system?
x: Prataparudra II is identified as the originator of the Kakatiya Nayankara system. The Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara system grew out of the Kakatiya system.

s: About how many nayakas held amarams under the Vijayanagara amara-nayankara system?
x: Vijayanagara had about 200 nayakas, against the Kakatiyas' 75 or 77.

s: The Kakatiya nayankara system had how many nayakas?
x: The Kakatiya system had 75 or 77 nayakas holding mandalams and forts; Vijayanagara had about 200.

s: From whom did the Palegars or Poligars primarily originate?
x: The Amara-nayakas became the Palegars or Poligars when central authority weakened after the Battle of Talikota.

s: The Palegars (Poligars), who became hereditary local rulers after Talikota, are regarded as the forerunners of whom?
x: The Palegars are regarded as forerunners of the zamindars; Ryotwari was introduced by Munro after suppressing them.

s: Which system did Thomas Munro introduce after suppressing the poligars of Rayalaseema?
x: Munro, with military officer Campbell, suppressed the poligars and then brought in the Ryotwari system.

s: Which British officer, assisted by Campbell, crushed the Palegars of Rayalaseema?
x: Thomas Munro, with his officer Campbell, crushed the Palegars and then introduced the Ryotwari system.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mera was the share of the harvest given to the Ayagars.
2. Meruka was a tax on sale and purchase.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share and Meruka was the sale and purchase tax, so both statements are correct.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to land classification is correctly matched?
x: Bagayati denoted garden land. Nanja was wet land, Punja was dry land and Banjara was waste land.

s: What did Neerarambamu or Magani denote in the Andhra terminology of Vijayanagara revenue administration?
o: Garden land assessed through market tolls
x: Neerarambamu, also called Magani, was irrigated land and was generally taxed in grain at higher rates.

s: How were the rights to collect market or santhalu taxes generally given in the Vijayanagara Empire?
o: Assigned permanently to village assemblies without payment
x: The right to collect market taxes was auctioned to Sunkandarlu.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Putrodaya kanuka — Sale and purchase of goods
x: Putrodaya kanuka was a tax on the birth of a son. Sale and purchase of goods was taxed through Meruka.

s: Which of the following statements regarding Siddhaya is correct?
o: It was exclusively a military title of the commander-in-chief.
It denoted a fixed levy, with varieties connected with occupations such as cotton ginning and toddy tapping.
It was the name of the royal treasury.
It referred only to a tax on sale and purchase of goods.
x: Siddhaya meant a fixed levy. Pinje Siddhayam was connected with cotton ginners, Eidipi Siddhayam with toddy tappers and Jati Siddhayam with castes or professions.

s: On whom was the Vijayanagara tax Navidadere levied?
x: Navidadere (Kondaju) was the barbers' tax; Maneyanna was the house tax.

s: On what was the Vijayanagara tax Maneyanna (Illari Pannu) levied?
x: Maneyanna was the house tax.

s: What was the usual share of produce collected as land revenue in Vijayanagara?
x: The usual share was 1/6; fertile land paid 1/4 or 1/3.

s: Which Vijayanagara tax was levied on the birth of a son?
x: Putrodaya Kanuka was levied on the birth of a son; Kalyana Kanika was the wedding tax.

s: Which Vijayanagara ruler totally withdrew (abolished) the marriage tax?
x:
Most books and keys (Rocket, NextGen previous papers, APPSC G1 2010): Krishnadevaraya. Some keys and the old notes: Sadasiva Raya.
Krishnadevaraya totally withdrew the marriage tax (first remitted under Saluva Narasimha); the Sadasiva-period (Rama Raya) inscriptions record the remission of the barbers' tax. (Old key Sadasiva Raya.)

s: Which tax of the Vijayanagara period was levied on sale and purchase?
x: Meruka was the tax on sale and purchase; Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share and Merulu the Talari's grain gifts.

s: What were the land-tax documents of the Vijayanagara period called?
x: Land-tax documents of the Vijayanagara period were called Adhuvanatantram.

s: Which Vijayanagara ruler first remitted the marriage tax?
x: Saluva Narasimha first remitted the marriage tax; Krishnadevaraya later withdrew it totally.

s: Through which work did the Vijayanagara judicial system follow the Yajnavalkya and Parashara Smritis?
x: The Yajnavalkya and Parashara Smritis were followed through Madhavacharya’s Parashara Madhaviyam.

s: What did Himsodbhava and Dhanodbhava respectively refer to in the Vijayanagara judicial system?
x: Himsodbhava referred to criminal cases, whereas Dhanodbhava referred to civil cases.

s: What was the punishment for theft in the Vijayanagara period?
x: Theft was punished by mutilation and treason by death; Brahmins received life imprisonment instead of death.

s: Who policed the village under the Vijayanagara Kavali system?
x: The Talari policed the village, the Peta Kavalidaru the towns and the Kavali Daru the Sthala.

s: What punishment did a Brahmin guilty of a crime punishable by death receive in the Vijayanagara period?
x: Brahmins got life imprisonment instead of death.

s: Who policed the Sthala level under the Kavali system?
x: Talari policed the village, Kavali Daru the sthala and Peta Kavalidaru the towns.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Vijayanagara Kavali system:
1. The Talari policed the village.
2. The Kavali Daru policed the towns.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Talari policed the village; towns were policed by the Peta Kavalidaru, while the Kavali Daru worked at the sthala level.

s: Who was the Pradvivaka in the Vijayanagara administration?
o: A judge who advised the king and explained legal texts
The head of the village police
The officer in charge of the treasury
The commander of the hill forts
x: The Pradvivaka was the judge and adviser who helped the king in justice and explained the legal texts.

s: Who headed a Nadu or Seema in Vijayanagara provincial administration?
x: A Nadu was under the Nadagauda and Parupatyagar; a Rajya under a prince or Durgadhipati, a Sthala under the Reddi/Gauda/Sthalakaranam and a village under the Ayagars.

s: Which of the following statements about Vijayanagara provincial governors is correct?
o: They could not keep their own armies
They held office for life without transfer
x: Governors could mint coins, levy taxes and keep armies, but they were frequently transferred.

s: What title did the Sangama princes who governed Vijayanagara provinces hold?
x: Princes governing a Rajya or Mandala under the Sangamas were titled Odeyar.

s: Before 1485, Saluva Narasimha was the governor of which Andhra rajya?
x: Saluva Narasimha governed Chandragiri before 1485; it later became a capital.

s: Which Andhra rajya became the new headquarters of Tirumala after Talikota?
x: After Talikota, Penukonda became Tirumala's new headquarters.

s: About how many rajyams were there under Achyutaraya?
x: There were about 17 rajyams under Achyutaraya.

s: Which officer of the nadu (sima) collected revenue and maintained forts in the Vijayanagara empire?
x: The Parupatyagar was the nadu/sima officer who collected revenue and maintained the forts.

s: Which was the most important Andhra rajya of the Vijayanagara empire, covering the Paka and Muliki districts (Nellore, Kadapa)?
x: Udayagiri was the most important Andhra rajya and was governed by royal princes under the first dynasty.

s: How many Ayagars traditionally ran each village under the Ayagar system?
x: Each village was administered by 12 hereditary Ayagars. They included officials, artisans and service providers.

s: How were the Ayagars generally paid?
o: A fixed share of customs duties alone
Tax-free Manyam lands and a share of the harvest called Mera
Regular cash salaries from the royal treasury only
x: Ayagars received tax-free Manyam lands, also called Mirasi, Bhattu Vrutti or Jatikattu Manyalu, along with a share of the harvest called Mera. They were not paid regular cash salaries.

s: Which of the following pairs (Ayagar – function) is correctly matched?
x: The Talari was the village watchman. The Karanam was the accountant, the Reddi the village head and the Purohita the priest.

s: Who was the 'Kase' among the village artisans of the Vijayanagara period?
x: Kase was the mason or house-builder; Vadrangi was the carpenter, Kummari the potter and Chakali the washerman.

s: Who collected the grain gifts called 'Merulu' in Vijayanagara villages?
x: The Talari (watchman) collected Merulu; Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share.

s: Which village officer kept the accounts and land and crop registers in Vijayanagara villages?
x: The Karanam kept accounts, land and crop registers and temple accounts; the Reddi was the village head.

s: Who supervised forced labour (vetti) in a Vijayanagara village?
x: The Begari supervised vetti (forced labour).

s: What was the village head called Reddi in Andhra known as in Karnataka?
x: The Reddi was the village head and revenue collector of Andhra; in Karnataka he was the Gauda.

s: The Vijayanagara king, though supreme head of state, was expected to act within Dharma and in consultation with whom?
x: The king was supreme head, commander and fountain of justice, but acted within Dharma and with ministerial counsel.

s: Which historian characterised the Vijayanagara empire as a 'segmentary state'?
x: Burton Stein called it a segmentary state, whereas Nilakanta Sastri described it as a military administration.

s: Which historian described the Vijayanagara state as a 'military administration'?
x: Nilakanta Sastri called it a military administration; Burton Stein called it a segmentary state.

s: What does Krishnadevaraya's Amuktamalyada advise the king to do regarding foreign merchants?
o: Treat them generously and encourage imports
Confine them to a single port
Bar them from the horse trade
x: Amuktamalyada advises improving harbours, encouraging imports and treating foreign merchants generously.

s: What does Krishnadevaraya's Amuktamalyada advise the king to do regarding forest tribes?
o: Win them over rather than merely crush them
x: Amuktamalyada combines devotion with statecraft and advises winning over forest tribes rather than merely crushing them.

s: According to Amuktamalyada, to whom should the bulk of the king's revenue go?
x: Amuktamalyada advises that the bulk of revenue go to the army.

s: According to Amuktamalyada, who should command the forts?
x: Krishnadevaraya's maxim was that Brahmins should command forts.

s: Which of the following is correctly stated regarding the contents of Amuktamalyada?
o: It refers to Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns and gives political advice, but does not trace a genealogy from Bukka.
It is exclusively a manual on fort construction.
It records the genealogy of the dynasty from Bukka but not Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns.
It contains no discussion of kingship or administration.
x: Amuktamalyada contains political maxims on rajaniti, kingship and administration and refers to Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns, but it gives no genealogy from Bukka to Krishnadevaraya (APPSC G2 2003).

s: Who headed the Siddha (standing) army of Vijayanagara?
x: The standing army was under the Dalavayi; Durga Dannayakas commanded forts.

s: Who was the first Vijayanagara king to use cannon?
x: Bukka I was the first Vijayanagara king to use cannon; firearms were associated with Turkish and Portuguese experts.

s: Through which ports did Vijayanagara mainly import Arabian and Persian horses?
x: Horses came via the west-coast ports Goa, Honnavar and Bhatkal; Portuguese and Arab merchants ran the trade.

s: Who introduced the Samugaris, or gunmen, into the Vijayanagara military system?
x: Saluva Narasimha introduced the Samugaris, or gunmen. Bukka I is associated with the first use of cannon by a Vijayanagara king.

s: What were the four types of forts in the Vijayanagara period?
x: The four types of forts were Giri (hill), Sthala (land), Jala (water) and Vana (forest) forts.

s: How often was the Siddha (standing) army of Vijayanagara paid?
x: The standing army was paid every four months.

s: Under whom were the forts placed in the Vijayanagara period?
x: The four kinds of forts were under Durga Dannayakas.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Abdur Razzaq was Persian, not Russian. Caesar Frederick was a Venetian Italian visitor who saw the ruined capital after Talikota in 1567.

s: Which of the following pairs (traveller – reign) is correctly matched?
x: Nuniz visited during Achyutaraya's reign. Nicolo de Conti came under Devaraya I, Abdur Razzaq under Devaraya II, and Paes and Barbosa under Krishnadevaraya.

s: Which of the following works are identified alongside foreign accounts as important sources for studying Vijayanagara?
x: Amuktamalyada and Rayavachakam are mentioned alongside foreign accounts as significant sources for understanding Vijayanagara history.

s: Who was Fernao Nuniz, who wrote an account of Vijayanagara under Achyutadeva Raya?
x: Fernao Nuniz was a Portuguese horse-trader who wrote an account of Vijayanagara under Achyutadeva Raya in the 16th century.

s: During whose reign did the Italian traveller Nicolo de Conti visit Vijayanagara (1420-21)?
x: Conti came under Devaraya I and recorded a 60-mile city circuit and an army of 90,000.

s: Who was the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara?
x: Ibn Battuta of Morocco came under Harihara I; Nicolo Conti was the earliest European visitor.

s: From which country did Athanasius Nikitin, author of 'Journey Beyond Three Seas', come?
x: Nikitin was Russian and visited the Bahmani kingdom; Abdur Razzaq was Persian.

s: In which year did Caesar Frederick, who saw the ruined capital after Talikota, visit Vijayanagara?
x: Caesar Frederick of Venice came in 1567, under Sadasiva.

s: In which work did Robert Sewell translate the accounts of Paes and Nuniz?
x: Robert Sewell translated them in A Forgotten Empire (1900).

s: As whose envoy did Abdur Razzaq visit Vijayanagara?
x: Abdur Razzaq was the Timurid envoy of Shah Rukh and came in 1443.

s: In which year did Abdur Razzaq, the traveller who recorded 300 ports in the Vijayanagara empire, visit Vijayanagara?
x: Abdur Razzaq, envoy of Shah Rukh, came to the court of Devaraya II in 1443.

s: Who was the earliest European to visit Vijayanagara?
x: The Italian Nicolo de Conti (1420-21, under Devaraya I) was the earliest European visitor.

s: During whose reign did Ibn Battuta visit Vijayanagara?
x: Ibn Battuta of Morocco, the first foreign traveller to Vijayanagara, came under Harihara I.

s: Which kingdom did the Russian traveller Athanasius Nikitin visit?
x: Nikitin visited the Bahmani kingdom under Muhammad III and wrote Journey Beyond Three Seas.

s: Who wrote 'A Forgotten Empire' on Vijayanagara?
x: 'A Forgotten Empire' on Vijayanagara was written by Robert Sewell.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Duarte Barbosa — Religious freedom for all creeds
Domingo Paes — Journey Beyond Three Seas
x: Duarte Barbosa recorded religious freedom for all creeds. Journey Beyond Three Seas was written by Nikitin, Matla-us-Sadain by Abdur Razzaq, and the House of Victory was associated with Domingo Paes’s account.

s: Which traveller described Vijayanagara as being as large as Rome?
x: Domingo Paes, who came under Krishnadevaraya, compared the city to Rome and described the House of Victory.

s: Which traveller described Vijayanagara as a city 'the eye had not seen'?
x: Abdur Razzaq recorded this, along with the prostitution tax paid to the guards and the absence of purdah.

s: Barbosa observed that which communities lived without interference in the Vijayanagara Empire?
x: Barbosa recorded that Christians, Jews and Muslims lived without interference, indicating a measure of religious tolerance.

s: At what number did Nicolo de Conti estimate the Vijayanagara army?
x: Conti put the army at 90,000 and the city at 60 miles round; Nuniz gave 600,000 amara troops.

s: According to Abdur Razzaq, each of the 300 ports of the Vijayanagara empire was equal to which port?
x: Abdur Razzaq wrote that Vijayanagara had 300 ports, each equal to Calicut.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Traveller)
a. Abdur Razzaq
b. Domingo Paes
c. Duarte Barbosa
d. Nicolo Conti
List-II (Observation)
1. Religious freedom for all creeds
2. 300 ports, each equal to Calicut
3. City 60 miles round
4. City as large as Rome
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Abdur Razzaq recorded 300 ports, Paes compared the city to Rome, Barbosa noted religious freedom and Conti put the city at 60 miles round.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Nicolo Conti recorded the practice of Sati (sahagamana) in Vijayanagara.
2. Fernao Nuniz also recorded Sati and polygamy in Vijayanagara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both Nicolo Conti and Fernao Nuniz recorded Sati in Vijayanagara; Barbosa and Paes also mention it.

s: Which traveller recorded that women in Vijayanagara served as wrestlers, accountants, astrologers and even judges?
x: The Portuguese Fernao Nuniz (with Paes) recorded women working as wrestlers, accountants, astrologers, palanquin bearers and even judges.

s: Who wrote the Matla-us-Sadain?
x: The Persian envoy Abdur Razzaq described Vijayanagara under Devaraya II in his Matla-us-Sadain.

s: In which work did Abdur Razzaq record his visit to Vijayanagara?
x: Abdur Razzaq wrote the Matla-us-Sadain; Journey Beyond Three Seas is Nikitin's work.

s: Which foreign traveller wrote a dynastic history of Vijayanagara, including its foundation legend?
x: Fernao Nuniz, a Portuguese horse dealer, wrote on the dynasty's history and foundation legend.

s: According to Fernao Nuniz, how many amara troops did the Vijayanagara nayakas maintain?
x: Nuniz put the amara troops at 600,000; Conti put the army at 90,000.

s: Which traveller recorded that 250 buffaloes and 400 goats were sacrificed on the last day of Mahanavami?
x: Domingo Paes recorded the Mahanavami sacrifices.

s: Which of the following irrigation works is correctly matched with its ruler?
o: Bukka I — Siruveru tank near Penukonda
x: Bukka I is associated with the Siruveru tank near Penukonda. Narasambudhi was associated with Saluva Narasimha, while the Toragallu and Kambham works belonged to Krishnadevaraya.

s: Who issued the Porumamilla inscription, which lays down 12 rules (Dwadasa Sutras) for building a tank?
x: The Porumamilla inscription, with its 12 rules (Dwadasa Sutras) for building a tank, was issued by Bhaskara (Bhaskara Bhavadura), son of Bukka I and prince of Udayagiri. It records the Anantasagaram tank (1369) in Kadapa; it was not issued by Krishnadevaraya.

s: What was the temple treasury kept by the Karanam called in the Vijayanagara period?
x: The temple treasury was the Sri Bhandara, kept by the Karanam; Devadaya villages were temple endowments.

s: Where did the merchant guilds (Samayas) of the Vijayanagara period usually meet?
x: The Samayas, led by the Ayyavali guild, met in temple mandapas, not royal palaces.

s: What was the main revenue of the Vijayanagara state?
x: Land tax was the main revenue source.

s: Who built the Siruveru tank near Penukonda?
x: Bukka I built the Siruveru tank; Saluva Narasimha built Narasambudhi.

s: Which inscription lays down twelve rules (Dwadasa Sutras) for building a tank?
x: The Porumamilla inscription of Bhaskara Bhavadura (1369) lays down the twelve rules for tank building.

s: In which present-day district is Porumamilla, whose inscription records the Anantasagaram tank, located?
x: Porumamilla, site of the 1369 inscription on the Anantasagaram tank, is in Kadapa district.

s: Who built the Narasambudhi tank in Anantapur?
x: Saluva Narasimha built the Narasambudhi tank; Bukka I built the Siruveru tank.

s: Which tank did Krishnadevaraya build with the help of Portuguese engineers?
x: Krishnadevaraya built the Nagalapuram tank with Portuguese engineers, besides the Toragallu dam and Kambham tank.

s: Tank-building was counted among the Saptasantanas. What were the Saptasantanas?
x: The Saptasantanas were the seven meritorious acts, and tank-building was one of them.

s: What were 'Devadaya' in the Vijayanagara period?
x: Devadaya were temple villages or endowments; Sri Bhandara was the temple treasury.

s: Which of the following pairs (group – occupation) is correctly matched?
x: The Kaikkolars were weavers, like the Padmasalis. Vira Panchalas were artisans and Settis were traders.

s: Vijayanagara society is described as having four varnas and about how many castes?
x: Society had four varnas and about eighteen castes; Brahmins included Vaidikas and Niyogis and many Sudras became amaranayakas.

s: Who were the Vira Panchalas in Vijayanagara society?
x: The Vira Panchalas worked in gold, iron, brass, wood and stone.

s: Who were the Niyogis in Vijayanagara society?
x: Niyogis were Brahmin officials; Vaidikas were priests.

s: Which of the following groups of Vijayanagara society were traders?
x: Settis, Komatis and Balijas were the trading groups; Vira Panchalas were artisans, Kaikkolars weavers and Vaidikas/Niyogis Brahmins.

s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Valangai and Idangai divisions in Vijayanagara society?
o: Valangai consisted exclusively of Brahmins, whereas Idangai consisted of royal officials
Valangai consisted mainly of agricultural and trading groups, whereas Idangai consisted mainly of artisans and some traders
Valangai consisted mainly of artisans, whereas Idangai consisted exclusively of priests
Both Valangai and Idangai consisted only of agricultural communities
x: Valangai or right-hand groups were mainly agricultural and trading communities. Idangai or left-hand groups were mainly artisans, including Panchala smiths, along with some traders.

s: The Valangai and Idangai caste groupings of the Vijayanagara period had their origin in which earlier period?
x: The right-hand and left-hand groupings began during Chola times and continued under the Vijayanagara Empire.

s: Which groups mainly made up the Idangai (left-hand) division of Vijayanagara society?
x: Idangai were mainly artisans (including Panchala smiths); Valangai were agricultural and trading groups.

s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of east-coast ports associated with the Vijayanagara period?
x: Pulicat, Mylapore, Motupalli and Machilipatnam were east-coast ports. The other groups contain west-coast ports.

s: What was the chief export of the Vijayanagara empire?
x: Kalamkari was the chief export; horses were the chief import and Chinese silk was also imported.

s: Where were the diamonds mined in Kurnool and Anantapur polished in the Vijayanagara period?
x: Diamonds were polished at Vajrakarur; Gutti and Rayadurg supplied silk and Venkatagiri zari.

s: Of which industry were Tadipatri, Adoni and Gutti Vijayanagara centres?
x: Tadipatri, Adoni and Gutti were textile centres; Vajrakarur was known for diamonds.

s: Which of the following was a west-coast port of the Vijayanagara period?
x: Bhatkal was on the west coast; Pulicat, Motupalli and Machilipatnam were east-coast ports.

s: For what was Venkatagiri known in the Vijayanagara period?
x: Venkatagiri was known for zari; Gutti and Rayadurg for silk.

s: The Motupalli Dharma Sasanam (1416) is linked with which ruler, who took Motupalli?
x: Devaraya I took Motupalli; the Motupalli Dharma Sasanam dates to 1416.

s: With what was Vajrakarur associated in the Vijayanagara period?
x: Vajrakarur is associated with diamonds; Pulicat, Motupalli and Machilipatnam were important Andhra ports.

s: What was the chief import of the Vijayanagara empire?
x: Horses were the chief import; Kalamkari was the chief export and diamonds and sugar were also exported.

s: Which places were centres of silk production in the Vijayanagara period?
x: Gutti and Rayadurg were silk centres; Vajrakarur polished diamonds.

s: Which Vijayanagara ruler of the Aravidu dynasty allowed a church to be established at Chandragiri and protected the Jesuit mission?
x: Venkatapati Raya II allowed a church at Chandragiri and extended protection to the Jesuit mission.

s: From the reign of which ruler did Venkateswara replace Virupaksha as the main deity?
x: From Venkatapati II onward, Venkateswara replaced Virupaksha as the main deity.

s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of Shaiva centres?
x: Srisailam, Tripurantakam and Srikalahasti were Shaiva centres. Kanchi, Mangalagiri and Pushpagiri and Tirupati, Ahobilam and Kadiri were Vaishnava centres, and the last group is mixed.

s: Who built the Mahanavami or Dasara Dibba at Vijayanagara?
x: The Mahanavami Dibba, on which the Dasara celebrations were held, was built by Krishnadevaraya.

s: Who was the family deity of the Sangama dynasty?
x: The Shaivite Sangamas had Virupaksha as family deity; their family guru was Kalamukha Kriya Shakti.

s: For temples of which deity were Ahobilam and Kadiri known?
x: Ahobilam and Kadiri had Narasimha temples; Tirupati rose under Saluva Narasimha.

s: From where did Narahari Tirtha spread the Dvaita philosophy?
x: Narahari Tirtha spread Dvaita from Srikurmam, not Sringeri.

s: Who was the guru of the Sangama rulers?
x: The Shaiva Sangamas had Kalamukha Kriya Shakti as guru and Virupaksha as family deity.

s: Which Vijayanagara ruler enlisted Muslims in the army and built a mosque?
x: Devaraya II enlisted Muslims in the army with jagirs and built a mosque.

s: Under which ruler did Tirupati rise to prominence?
x: Tirupati rose under Saluva Narasimha, as the later dynasties were Vaishnava.

s:
Consider the following statements about Christian missions under Vijayanagara:
1. Venkatapati Raya II allowed a church at Chandragiri.
2. Venkatapati Raya II belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Venkatapati Raya II allowed the Chandragiri church and protected the Jesuit mission, but he was an Aravidu ruler.

s: Which place in West Godavari was the main seat of Vasavi Kanyaka Parameswari, the goddess of the Arya Vysyas?
x: Penugonda in West Godavari is the seat of Vasavi Kanyaka Parameswari; Penukonda in Anantapur was the later Vijayanagara capital.

s: In which work of Krishnadevaraya does Vasantotsava, the spring festival, appear?
x: Vasantotsava appears in Jambavati Parinayam; Paes and Abdur Razzaq described the Mahanavami.

s: To which ritual did Burton Stein compare the Vijayanagara Mahanavami festival?
x: Stein compared the Mahanavami to an Ashvamedha; nayakas brought tribute and the financial year began with it.

s: With which festival did the Vijayanagara financial year begin?
x: The financial year began with Mahanavami, when the nayakas brought tribute.

s: Which one of the following statements about devadasis in Vijayanagara society is correct?
o: They were military officers appointed as amaranayakas.
They were exclusively palace slaves without religious functions.
They were temple dancers trained in music and dance and could be land-owning and respected.
They were Brahmin officials known as Niyogis.
x: Devadasis were temple dancers trained in music and dance; many were land-owning and socially respected. Domingo Paes described them.

s: Which social practice did the term 'Benabaga' denote in Vijayanagara society?
x: “Benabaga” is used in connection with the existence of slavery in Vijayanagara society.

s: What did 'Varashulkam' mean in Vijayanagara society?
x: Varashulkam was dowry, while Kanyashulkam was bride price.

s: Which of the following was generally NOT practised among women in Vijayanagara society?
x: Strict purdah was not generally practised; women served as bodyguards and wrestlers, and both kanyasulkam and dowry existed.

s: Which of the following women are specifically mentioned as learned women of the Vijayanagara period?
x: Gangadevi and Tirumalamba are identified as learned women of the Vijayanagara period.

s:
Consider the following statements about social terms of the Vijayanagara period:
1. Kanyashulkam meant bride price.
2. Varashulkam meant slavery.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Kanyashulkam was bride price; Varashulkam meant dowry, and Benabaga meant slavery.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women in Vijayanagara society?
o: Women served as bodyguards and wrestlers
x: There was no strict purdah; the other three statements are correct.

s: Which form of marriage was the most popular in Vijayanagara society?
x: Brahma vivaha, in which the father gives his daughter to a suitable groom, was the most popular form.

s: According to the Burhan-i-Maasir, what was Sadasiva Raya's yearly income?
x: The Nizam Shahi chronicle Burhan-i-Maasir put Sadasiva Raya's yearly income at 12 crore huns.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Varaha — Silver coin equal to one-sixth of a panam
Pratapa — Gold coin equal to half a varaha
Jital — Gold coin, the largest denomination
x: Pratapa was a gold coin equal to half a varaha and was called Mada in Telugu. Varaha was the largest gold coin, panam was gold, and jital was copper.

s: Which was the most used coin in the Vijayanagara empire?
x: The panam was the most used coin; Europeans called the varaha the pagoda, and Mada was the Telugu name of the pratapa.

s: On whose coins does the Garuda symbol appear?
x: Garuda appears on Achyutaraya's coins; Hanuman on those of Harihara and Bukka, Venkateswara and Balakrishna on Krishnadevaraya's and Varaha on Tirumala Raya's.

s: Which gold coin was the largest denomination of Vijayanagara coinage?
x: The varaha (pagoda) was the largest gold coin; Tar and Pesado were silver and Jital and Kasu copper.

s: Of which metal was the Tar coin of Vijayanagara made?
x: Tar and Pesado were silver; Jital and Kasu were copper.

s: Which of the following pairs (coin – metal) is NOT correctly matched?
x: Pesado, like the Tar, was a silver coin; the other pairs are correct.

s: What was the Pratapa (Mada) coin of Vijayanagara worth?
x: The gold Pratapa was half a varaha; the panam was one-tenth of a pratapa.

s: By which other names was the Vijayanagara gold coin Varaha known?
x: The Varaha, the largest gold coin, was also called Pagoda, Gadyana or Honnu; Mada was the Pratapa.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Coin symbol)
a. Hanuman
b. Venkateswara and Balakrishna
c. Garuda
d. Varaha
List-II (Ruler)
1. Tirumala Raya
2. Achyutaraya
3. Krishnadevaraya
4. Harihara and Bukka
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Hanuman appears on coins of Harihara and Bukka, Venkateswara and Balakrishna on Krishnadevaraya's, Garuda on Achyutaraya's and Varaha on Tirumala Raya's.

s: How many musical pillars does the Vittala Ranga mandapa have?
x: The Vittala Ranga mandapa has 56 musical pillars, not 108.

s: Which is regarded as the first and largest temple of Hampi?
x: The Virupaksha temple, on the Tungabhadra and dedicated to Shiva as Pampapati, is the first and largest temple of Hampi.

s: Which Hampi temple is popularly known as the Saptaswara Devalayam?
x: Saptaswara Devalayam is the Vitthala temple; the Virupaksha temple is associated with Pampapati.

s: Who enlarged the Virupaksha temple at Hampi under Devaraya II?
x: Lakkana Dandesha enlarged it under Devaraya II; Krishnadevaraya added the central pillared hall and eastern gopuram in 1510.

s: To which Hampi temple do the musical pillars and the stone chariot belong?
x: Musical pillars and the stone chariot belong to the Vitthala temple; the Hazara Rama has Hoysala-style pillars and Ramayana friezes.

s: Under which ruler was the Vaishnava Vitthala Temple at Hampi begun?
x: The Vitthala Temple was begun under Devaraya II and expanded by Krishnadevaraya.

s: Which Hampi temple was the royal chapel of Krishnadeva Raya, with Ramayana friezes?
x: The Hazara Rama was Krishnadeva Raya's royal chapel; Virupaksha is linked with Lakkana Dandesha.

s: The Tiruvengalanatha (Achyutaraya) temple at Hampi was set up in 1534 by which officer?
x: Achyutaraya's officer Hiriya Tirumalaraja set up the temple in 1534; Lakkana Dandesha enlarged Virupaksha.

s: In which year did Krishnadevaraya add the eastern gopuram of the Virupaksha temple at Hampi?
x: Krishnadevaraya added the eastern gopuram of the Virupaksha temple in 1510.

s: From where did Krishnadevaraya bring the Bala Krishna idol of the Krishna temple at Hampi?
x: Krishnadevaraya brought the Bala Krishna idol from the Udayagiri fort.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to Hampi is correctly matched?
o: Virupaksha temple – enlarged by Lakkana Dandesha
x: Lakkana Dandesha enlarged the Virupaksha temple under Devaraya II; Hazara Rama is Krishnadevaraya's, the Achyutaraya temple dates to 1534, and Pampapati is Virupaksha.

s: What is the popular name of the Virupaksha temple at Hampi?
x: The Virupaksha (Shiva) temple, the first and largest at Hampi, is popularly called Pampapati.

s: To which deity is the Achyutaraya temple at Hampi dedicated?
x: The Achyutaraya temple (1534) is dedicated to Tiruvengalanatha, a form of Vishnu.

s: Which of the following at Hampi is credited to Krishnadevaraya?
o: Enlargement of the Virupaksha temple by Lakkana Dandesha
x: Krishnadevaraya made the Ugra Narasimha, Hanuman statue and monolithic Ganesha; the other works belong to Achyutaraya's and Devaraya II's reigns.

s: Which of the following pairs (temple – place) is correctly matched?
x: The Vitthala Temple is at Hampi. The Hoysaleswara Temple is at Halebidu, Matangeshvara at Khajuraho and Vimal Vasahi at Mount Abu.

s: Which Rashtrakuta king built the Kailasa Temple at Ellora?
x: Krishna I built the Kailasa Temple; Vimal Vasahi was built by Vimal Shah and Dhanga is linked with the Matangeshvara Temple.

s: Which of the following pairs (temple – patron) is correctly matched?
x: The Kailasa Temple goes with Krishna I. Narasimha I goes with the Hoysaleswara Temple, Vishnuvardhana with Chennakeshava and Vimal Shah with Vimal Vasahi.

s: With the reign of which ruler is the Lepakshi temple (c. 1530s) associated?
x: The Lepakshi temple was built c. 1530-40 by the Nayaka brothers Virupanna and Veeranna of Penukonda, officers of Achyutaraya, so it belongs to Achyutaraya's reign.

s: Which Nayaka brothers built the Veerabhadra temple at Lepakshi?
x: It was built by Virupanna and Veeranna of Penukonda on Kurma Shailam, not by Harihara and Bukka.

s: What is the Naga linga at Lepakshi?
o: A linga carved from a single boulder and sheltered by a seven-hooded serpent
A linga placed inside the stone chariot
A linga carved on the walls of the Ramachandra temple
A bronze linga installed by Krishnadevaraya
x: The Naga linga is carved from a single boulder and is sheltered by a seven-hooded serpent.

s: Which one of the following places is located in Sri Sathya Sai district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Lepakshi is located in Sri Sathya Sai district. The other listed places are associated with different locations in Andhra Pradesh.

s: On what does Lepakshi's fame for Vijayanagara school paintings rest?
x: Lepakshi's painting fame comes from its ceiling murals; the huge monolithic Nandi is a separate attraction.

s: On which hill does the Veerabhadra temple at Lepakshi stand?
x: The Lepakshi Veerabhadra temple stands on Kurma Shailam hill near Hindupur.

s: To whom are the three shrines of the Lepakshi temple complex dedicated?
x: Lepakshi has shrines of Shiva, Veerabhadra and Vishnu, each with a mukha mandapa.

s: Where is the largest monolithic Nandi in India?
x: Lepakshi's monolithic Nandi is the largest in India (APPSC G2 2017).

s: Which temple is famous for its 'hanging pillar'?
x: The hanging pillar is at Lepakshi (APPSC 2019).

s: The serpent over the Naga linga at Lepakshi has how many hoods?
x: The Naga linga is a linga under a seven-hooded serpent, carved from a single boulder.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Lepakshi temple:
1. It lies in Sri Sathya Sai district.
2. Its builders were governors of Chandragiri.
3. It was built c. 1530-40 under Achyutaraya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Lepakshi is in Sri Sathya Sai district and was built c. 1530-40 under Achyutaraya; its builders Virupanna and Veeranna were governors of Penukonda.

s: Near which town is the Lepakshi temple located?
x: The Lepakshi Veerabhadra temple stands on Kurma Shailam hill near Hindupur, Sri Sathya Sai district.

s: By what other name is the Veerabhadra temple at Lepakshi known?
x: The Lepakshi Veerabhadra temple is also called the Papanaseswara temple.

s: Where was the state launch of Yogandhra-2026 held on 8 June 2026?
x: The state launch of Yogandhra-2026 was held at Lepakshi on 8 June 2026.

s: Themes from which works are depicted on the ceilings of the Lepakshi temple?
x: The ceilings show Ramayana and Mahabharata themes, while the walls carry Shiva subjects such as Parvati Parinayamu and Tripurasura Samharam.

s: Which place is famous for 'pictorial inscriptions' in the Vijayanagara style?
x: Lepakshi, with the finest Vijayanagara-school murals, is famous for 'pictorial inscriptions'. Tadipatri is known for its gopurams, Ahobilam for Narasimha temples and Chandragiri for its fort.

s: What do the murals at the Virupaksha temple at Hampi depict?
o: The campaigns of the Aravidu rulers
The life of Buddha and Jataka stories
x: The Hampi Virupaksha temple murals include the Dashavatara and Girijakalyana themes.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Vijayanagara mural painting?
o: Mineral pigments such as ochre, green, black and white were used
The figures lacked movement and were rigidly proportioned
The paintings were executed on lime plaster
Bold dark outlines and flat colours were characteristic
x: Vijayanagara murals had elongated figures and energetic movement, so the claim that they lacked movement is false.

s: Who wrote A Survey of Painting in the Deccan, identified as a key source for the study of Vijayanagara painting?
x: Stella Kramrisch wrote A Survey of Painting in the Deccan.

s: Where are the wall murals of Parvati Parinayamu and Tripurasura Samharam found?
x: Lepakshi's walls show Shiva themes such as Parvati Parinayamu and Tripurasura Samharam.

s: In which year was the 'Group of Monuments at Hampi' inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: The Group of Monuments at Hampi became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

s: Which Hampi monument appears on the reverse of the Rs 50 note (Mahatma Gandhi New series)?
x: The Vittala stone chariot is on the reverse of the Rs 50 note.

s: Around which Hampi temple did the area called the 'Athens of Vijayanagara' lie?
x: The area around the Virupaksha temple, the first and largest temple of Hampi, was called the 'Athens of Vijayanagara'.

s: In which present-day district of Karnataka is Hampi located?
x: Hampi, on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra, is in Vijayanagara district of Karnataka.

s: According to Domingo Paes, why did the walls of Vijayanagara enclose fields and gardens?
o: To separate the royal centre from temples
x: Paes noted that the walls enclosed agricultural tracts so the city could withstand sieges.

s: Tadipatri, a centre of the Vijayanagara style, lies in which district?
x: Tadipatri is in Anantapur; Lepakshi is in Sri Sathya Sai district.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Largest monolithic Nandi in India — Lepakshi
Gopurams surpassing those of Hampi Vittala temple — Chandragiri
x: The gopurams said by art critics to surpass those of Hampi's Vittala temple are at Tadipatri, not Chandragiri. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: With whom is the mukha mandapam of the Mallikarjuna Temple at Srisailam associated?
x: Harihara II is associated with the mukha mandapam at Srisailam; Saluva Narasimha began the Vijayanagara patronage of Tirupati.

s: At which place are the temples credited to the Pemmasani Nayakas?
x: The Pemmasani Nayakas are credited with the Tadipatri temples, not Tirupati.

s: In which year did the gali gopuram at Srikalahasti collapse?
x: Krishnadevaraya renovated Srikalahasti; its gali gopuram collapsed in 2010.

s: Which temple is noted for four entrance gates facing the four directions?
x: Among these, Srisailam is noted for its four entrance gates facing the four directions.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Chintala Venkataramana and Bugga Ramalingeswara — Tadipatri
Upper and Lower Narasimha Temples — Kadiri
x: The Chintala Venkataramana and Bugga Ramalingeswara temples are at Tadipatri. The Upper and Lower Narasimha temples are at Ahobilam (not Kadiri), Mallikarjuna is the deity of Srisailam (not Tirupati), and Venkateswara is the deity of Tirupati (not Ahobilam).

s: Who is the presiding deity of the Ahobilam temples?
x: Ahobilam's Upper and Lower temples are dedicated to Narasimha.

s: The Srikalahasti temple enshrines which linga?
x: Srikalahasti is the Vayu linga shrine.

s: Who built the Chintala Venkataramana temple at Tadipatri?
x: Pemmasani Timmanayudu built it in the mid-16th century.

s: Kadiri, an early centre of the Narasimha cult, has a temple of which deity?
x: Kadiri's temple is dedicated to Narasimha.

s: Where are the high-relief sculpture (Ubattu Shilpalu) and the painting of Vatapatra Shayi found?
x: Tadipatri has Ubattu Shilpalu and the painting of Vatapatra Shayi.

s: Where is the Bugga Ramalingeswara temple located?
x: Bugga Ramalingeswara is at Tadipatri, credited to the Pemmasani Nayakas.

s: In which district is the Ontimitta Kodandarama temple located?
x: The Vijayanagara-era Kodandarama temple of Ontimitta is in Kadapa district.

s: Which temple is the venue of Andhra Pradesh's official Sri Rama Navami celebrations?
x: Ontimitta Kodandarama temple, linked with Pothana, is the venue of AP's official Sri Rama Navami; Bhadrachalam is now in Telangana.

s: In March 2026, inscriptions of Achyutaraya (1534 CE) were found on a 50-ft monolithic pillar of which temple?
x: The 1534 CE inscriptions were found on the 50-ft monolithic pillar of the Somapalayam Chennakesava temple in Annamayya district.

s: With whom was the sculptured prakaram at Srisailam associated?
o: Shanti Lingayya during the time of Krishnadevaraya
x: Shanti Lingayya constructed the sculptured prakaram at Srisailam during the reign of Krishnadevaraya.

s: With whom are the steps to Tirumala and the Govindaraja temple associated?
x: They were associated with Anantaraju; Krishnadevaraya added the Kalyana mandapam, outer prakara and bronze statues.

s: To whom are the Tirumala Kalyana mandapam and the bronze statues of the king with Chinnadevi and Tirumaladevi credited?
x: Krishnadevaraya added these at Tirumala; Harihara II built the Srisailam mukha mandapam.

s:
Consider the following statements about Vijayanagara additions at Srisailam and Tirupati:
1. The Srisailam mukha mandapam is credited to Harihara II.
2. The sculptured prakaram at Srisailam is credited to Shanti Lingayya.
3. The steps to Tirumala are credited to Krishnadevaraya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The mukha mandapam is Harihara II's and the prakaram Shanti Lingayya's; the steps to Tirumala are credited to the Aravidu feudatory Anantaraju.

s: What was the 'kalyana mandapa' in Vijayanagara temple architecture?
o: Hall of composite pillars with yalis
x: The kalyana mandapa was the marriage hall; the Raya gopuram was the towering gateway and the Amman shrine the goddess's shrine.

s: Which statement regarding Vijayanagara secular architecture is correct?
o: The period introduced secular buildings inside temple premises.
The period used only wooden structures for royal buildings.
The period excluded all Indo-Islamic architectural influence.
Secular structures were confined exclusively to forts outside temple areas.
x: The Vijayanagara period introduced secular buildings within temple premises, while also showing Indo-Islamic influence in structures such as the Lotus Mahal and Huzur Daftar.

s: What is the towering gateway that dwarfs the central shrine in Vijayanagara architecture called?
x: The Raya gopuram is the towering gateway that dwarfs the central shrine.

s: What is a separate goddess shrine in a Vijayanagara temple complex, as at Hazara Rama, called?
x: The Amman shrine is the separate goddess shrine, seen at the Hazara Rama temple.

s: What are the thousand-pillared halls with carved composite pillars in Vijayanagara temples called?
x: Sahasra Stambha Mandapas are thousand-pillared halls with carved composite pillars.

s: Who described Vijayanagara architecture as the 'matured state of the Dravidian tradition'?
x: Percy Brown called it the matured state of the Dravidian tradition; Kramrisch surveyed Deccan painting.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Vijayanagara style:
1. Secular buildings were raised inside temple premises.
2. Pillared corridors were added to older temples.
3. The Ekapaadam was a Chola-type single pillar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Secular buildings in temple premises and added pillared corridors were new; the Ekapaadam was a Hoysala-type pillar.

s: With which ruler are the Mahanavami Dibba and the Lotus (Padma) Mahal at Hampi associated?
x: Krishnadevaraya's building at Hampi included the Ugra Narasimha, Hanuman statue, monolithic Ganesha, Mahanavami Dibba and Lotus Mahal.

s: By what other names is the Lotus Mahal at Hampi known?
x: The Lotus Mahal is also called Chitrangi or Padma Mahal.

s: What was the Huzur Daftar, or Diwan Khana, at Vijayanagara?
o: Stepped tank in the royal enclosure
Council chamber in Indo-Persian style with 40 pillars
Temple hall for divine marriage with 56 musical pillars
Royal bath with a lotus-shaped dome
x: Huzur Daftar or Diwan Khana was a council chamber in Indo-Persian style and had 40 pillars.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Lotus Mahal — Lotus-shaped structure with domes and Indo-Islamic influence
Huzur Daftar — Stepped tank in the royal enclosure
Queen's Bath — Council chamber with 40 pillars
Mahanavami Dibba — Elephant stables in the zenana area
x: The Lotus Mahal is lotus-shaped with domes in Indo-Islamic (Indo-Arabic) style. The Huzur Daftar was the 40-pillared council chamber (not a stepped tank), the Queen's Bath stood near the Lotus Mahal in the zenana area (it was not a council chamber), and the Mahanavami Dibba was the platform for the Dasara festival (not elephant stables).

s: Near which structure does the Queen's Bath (Maharani Snanavatika) at Hampi stand?
x: The Queen's Bath is near the Lotus Mahal, in the zenana area.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the secular structures of Hampi?
o: The Lotus Mahal shows Indo-Islamic influence
The Huzur Daftar is an Indo-Persian council chamber
The Mahanavami Dibba was built by Krishnadevaraya for Dasara
The Lotus Mahal is credited to Achyutaraya
x: The Lotus Mahal is credited to Krishnadevaraya, not Achyutaraya.

s: How many pillars did the Huzur Daftar (Diwan Khana) at Vijayanagara have?
x: The Indo-Persian Huzur Daftar had 40 pillars; 56 is the count of Vittala's musical pillars.

s: Sangita Suryodaya was written by a court musician of which Vijayanagara ruler?
x: Sangita Suryodaya was written by Lakshminarayana (Lakminatha), a court musician of Krishnadevaraya.

s: Which work was written by Bhandaru Lakshminarayana, the court musician of Krishnadevaraya?
x: Bhandaru Lakshminarayana, Krishnadevaraya's court musician, wrote Sangita Suryodaya.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with Udayagiri of Nellore?
o: Place where idols were looted by Mir Jumla
x: Udayagiri in Nellore was built by the Vijayanagara rulers, later taken by Golconda, and is associated with the Panchaloha cannon.

s: Under which ruler was Chandragiri the Aravidu capital?
x: Chandragiri served as the Aravidu capital under Venkatapati Raya II.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Aravidu capitals of the Vijayanagara Empire?
o: Vellore was the first Aravidu capital
x: Penukonda (1570) was first, followed by Chandragiri and then Vellore (1600), so Vellore was the last, not the first.

s: Whose base was Gooty (Gutti) fort?
x: Gooty was a stronghold and Aliya Rama Raya's base.

s: Where is the Raja Mahal, a blend of Hindu and Indo-Saracenic styles?
x: The Chandragiri fort has the Raja Mahal blending Hindu and Indo-Saracenic styles.

s: Which fort became the first Aravidu capital in 1570?
x: After Talikota, Penukonda became the first Aravidu capital in 1570.

s: Who looted the idols of Gandikota in 1657?
x: Mir Jumla looted the idols of Gandikota in 1657.

s: A record of which Vijayanagara ruler calls Gooty foremost among forts?
x: Gooty, one of AP's oldest hill forts, is called foremost among forts in a record of Bukka I.

s: Who wrote Sugriva Vijayam, regarded as the first Telugu Yakshagana?
x: Sugriva Vijayam is by Kandukuri Rudrakavi; Siddhendra Yogi founded Kuchipudi.

s: What was the earlier form of Yakshagana?
x: Koravanji was the earlier form of Yakshagana.

s: Whom did Yakshaganam mainly entertain under Vijayanagara?
x: Yakshaganam entertained the royal court and elites, while Tolu Bommalata was the chief rural entertainment.

s: Of which dance form is Veedhi Bhagavatham regarded as the forerunner?
x: Veedhi Bhagavatham is a street dance-drama regarded as the forerunner of Kuchipudi.

s: For whom was the leather shadow puppet show Tolu Bommalata the chief entertainment under Vijayanagara?
x: Tolu Bommalata entertained rural people; Yakshaganam entertained the court (APPSC 2019).

s: What role did folk performance traditions mainly play in the Andhra Movement?
o: Carry a distinct Telugu cultural consciousness to villages
x: Folk performance was living proof of a distinct Telugu culture and helped carry that cultural identity to the villages during the Andhra Movement.

s: Under which dynasty did Yakshaganam become folk theatre and Kuchipudi flourish?
x: In the Qutb Shahi period Yakshaganam became folk theatre and Kuchipudi flourished under Golconda.

s: Where was the leather puppet show Tholu Bommalata especially popular during the Vijayanagara period?
x: Tholu Bommalata was popular in rural Andhra, while Yakshaganam entertained royal courts and elites.

s: What was the ancient precursor of the Telugu Yakshagana?
x: Koravanji was the precursor of Yakshagana; Sugreeva Vijayam by Kandukuri Rudra Kavi is the first published Telugu Yakshaganam.

s: Which statement about the Yakshaganam of Andhra is correct?
o: It is a shepherd ballad sung to the Oggu drum.
It is performed in Telugu with elaborate costumes and Puranic stories.
It is a solo philosophical discourse.
It is performed only in Sanskrit, without costumes.
x: Andhra Yakshaganam is performed in Telugu, uses elaborate costumes and presents epic or Puranic stories.

s: Which is the first published Telugu Yakshaganam?
x: Sugreeva Vijayam by Kandukuri Rudra Kavi is the first published Telugu Yakshaganam.

s: Veedhi Natakam, the street dance-drama of Andhra, is the forerunner of which dance form?
x: Veedhi Natakam / Veedhi Bhagavatam is the forerunner of Kuchipudi.

s: Which community traditionally performed the Yakshaganam in Andhra?
x: Yakshaganam was performed by the Jakkula community; Jakkula Purandhri was its key female role.

s: Burrakatha developed from which tradition?
x: Burrakatha is a Telugu storytelling form from the Jangam Katha tradition.

s: Who is called the Pitamaha of Burrakatha?
x: Sheikh Nazar is the Pitamaha of Burrakatha; Narayana Dasu is the Harikatha Pitamaha.

s: Who wrote Mabhoomi, the hit play of the Praja Natya Mandali?
o: Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao
x: Mabhoomi was by Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao; the Mandali used folk plays to spread socialist ideals.

s: To whom did Burrakatha narrators chiefly carry news, reform ideas and nationalist messages?
x: Burrakatha narrators took news, reform and nationalist messages to unlettered rural populations, which made the form politically and socially useful.

s: Which place is regarded as the birthplace of Burrakatha?
x: Guntur is identified as the birthplace of Burrakatha, a folk form of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

s: Of whom does a traditional Burrakatha troupe generally consist?
o: Two narrators and one actor playing a king
A main narrator and two Vantalu
A single narrator accompanied by a chorus
Three dancers accompanied by two drummers
x: The standard Burrakatha group has three members: the main narrator in the middle and two Vantalu who respond and comment.

s: Which set of instruments is associated with Burrakatha?
x: Burrakatha uses the Gummata, Burra, Tambura and Ukki, with the characteristic chorus phrase 'Thandana Taana'.

s: Where was Burrakatha artist Sheikh Nazar born?
x: Nazar was born at Pannekallu in Guntur; his works include Palnati Yuddham and Bengal Karuvu.

s: With whom is the burrakatha 'Bengal Karuvu' associated?
x: Bengal Karuvu is Sheikh Nazar's; Sunkara Satyanarayana's works include Raithu Vijayam, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Veeresalingam.

s: Which folk form of Andhra Pradesh was earlier called 'Jangam Katha'?
x: Burrakatha was earlier called Jangam Katha (APPSC-GS 2018 key). It is also known as Jamukula Kathalu and as Thandana Katha in Rayalaseema. Harikatha is a solo form with Chidatalu, Oggu Katha is the Telangana shepherd ballad, and Pichukuntla Katha sings Palnati Veeracharitra.

s: By what name is Burrakatha called in Rayalaseema?
x: Burrakatha is known as Thandana Katha in Rayalaseema.

s: Besides Sheikh Nazar, which of the following popularised Burrakatha?
x: Burrakatha was popularised by Nazar, the Nittala Brothers and Bhadrakali.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Burrakatha?
o: Its earlier name was Jangam Katha
It is a solo form performed with Chidatalu
x: Burrakatha is a trio with burra, tambura and gummata; the solo form with Chidatalu is Harikatha.

s: Which art form is performed by a narrator with two Vantalu?
x: The trio of a narrator and two Vantalu is Burrakatha; Harikatha is a solo performance with Chidatalu.

s: Which organisation used folk plays such as Burrakatha to spread socialist ideals?
x: The Praja Natya Mandali used folk plays for socialist ideals; its hit play was Mabhoomi.

s: Who wrote the Burrakathas Kashtajeevi, Raithu Vijayam and Alluri Sitaramaraju?
x: Sunkara Satyanarayana wrote these Burrakathas and co-wrote Mabhoomi.

s: Who founded the Kuchipudi dance?
x: Kuchipudi grew from the Bhagavata Mela and was founded by Siddhendra Yogi.

s: Who founded Kuchipudi and from which tradition did it develop?
o: Founded by Sheikh Nazar and developed from Burrakatha
Founded by Siddhendra Yogi and developed from Bhagavata Mela
Founded by Adibhatla Narayana Dasu and developed from Harikatha
Founded by Vanarasa Govinda Rao and developed from Tolu Bommalata
x: Kuchipudi is traditionally associated with Siddhendra Yogi and grew out of the Bhagavata Mela dance-drama tradition.
